Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG4'APOLCOtvl Canter, EDSA corner Ouezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: l/wv.w. dilo.gov_ph SEC. ADELINO B. SITOY Presidential Legislative Liaison Office Office of the President Malacafiang, Manila Dear Sec. Sitoy: 3 0 MAR 201/ This has reference to your letter dated 25 January 2017 seeking for reconsideration or DI LG Opinion No. 26 dated 20 December 2016. It can be recalled that the assailed DILG Opinion was issued in response to your request Cor the enforcement of Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)'s Survey Result relative to boundary lines separating the Municipality of Cordova, Province of Cebu, from the City of Lapu-lapu. It was opined therein that the Department is without jurisdiction to enforce the DENR Boundaty Findings on the basis of Section 118 (d) of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 ", which refers the jurisdictional responsibility for settlement of boundary disputes to the respective sanggunians of the local government units concerned. In response to the said opinion is herein request for reconsideration anchored on grounds which we narrowed down into the fbllowing points of arguments: That there is no boundary dispute. This is supported by an argument that "there is only one official finding on the boundary that divides Mactan Island into the City of Lapu-lapu and the Municipality of Cordova, Cebu and that is the finding of DENR, Region VII, as contained in the Terminal Report Political Boundary Survey P b-07-00()058." Consequently, it was pointed out in the Ninth portion of the letter that Lavu-lapu City Mayor Radaza's refusal to recognize such DENR findings shall not be considered å "dispute" as it is not based on another government agency's findings, and such is purely oral and undocumented, to wit: "The refusal of Mayor Paz Corro Raclaza to sign the final map of the boundary and to recognize the factual findings of the DENR cannot be legally treated as basis for a "dispute" because:

11 1 . Mayor Radaza did not base her refusal and her contrary opinion on any findings by any other competent government agency; in fact, she did not base her refusal and her contrary opinion on any findings by any other competent government agency; in fact, she did not submit any document sufficient to controvert the official findings of the DENR. Her refusal was purely oral and undocumented. xxx" That the DENR had ruled to adopt the cadastral survey boundary of Lapu-lapu City as the municipal boundary line between Cordova and Lapu-lapu City irrespective of the relilsal of the Lapuaapu City Mayor to conform thereto. We shall answer these in one categorical and simultaneous discussion. A boundary dispute involving different local government units is defined in the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC). Specifically, Rule Ill, Article 15 thereof, states: "ARTICLE 15. Definition and Policy. — There is a boundary dispute when a portion or the whole of the ten-itorial area ofan LGUis claimed by two or more LGUs. XXN" In the case of Province of Antique and Municipality of Caluya vs. Hon. Calabocall the Supreme Court recognized the definition of the LGC on boundary dispute, it provides: "A boundary dispute involving different local government units is defined in the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code. Specifically, Rule Ill, Article 15 xxx. xxx a boundary dispute may involve "a portion or the whole" of a local government unit's territorial area. Nothing in this provision excludes a dispute over an island. So long as the island is being claimed by different local government units, there exists a boundary dispute." (Emphasis Supplied) Based on this definition, a boundary dispute arises when a portion or the whole of the territorial area of an LGU is claimed by two or more LGUJs. It is clear that this provision contemplates disagreement between LGUs concerning conflicting claims over their respective territories as a dispute in itself. Nothing in this provision requires that the respective claims of contending LGUs be based on findings of competent government agencies as a condition for a boundary dispute to be considered as such. Thus, mere disagreement suffices. Likewise, the same provision did not require that the boundary dispute be fully documented. 1 GR NO. 209146 dated June 8, 2016.

In addition thereto, we find no merit to the contention that the refusal to recognize the DENR Cadastral Survey Findings was purely oral and undocumented. The arguments presented did not support this position. In fact, the citations conferring the contents of' Terminal Report marked as Annex A and the Affidavit executed by Geodetic Engi neer/Contractor Fernando B. Gurrea, are contrary to the said contention. To emphasize, hereunder are the salient stipulations being referred to: . Item No. 8, Terminal Report on Political Boundary Survey (P "Annex A". "That on the first week of September the final Map was presented to the Hon. Mayor Paz Corro Radaza, however she refused to sign for reason that they were not amenable to the opinion of DENR and inform my Chief 01' Party that their Council will file a Resolution expressing their objection;"(Emphasis Supplied) Item No. 1 1, Ternlinal IReport' on Political Boundary Survey (Ph-07-000058), 2. "Annex A". "l l. After the posting period the Final Political Boundary map was prepared considering that no objections and comments were noted. Then the undersigned's staff seek the conformity of the mayor and adjacent mayor, however the City of Lapu-lapu expressed their disagreement thru its City Planning Officer. "(Emphasis Supplied) Item No. 13, Terminal Report on Political Boundary Survey 3. "Annex A". "On the said conference, the DENR ruled to adopt the approved cadastral survey boundary of Lapu-lapu as the Municipal Boundary line between Cordova and Lapu-lapu City, however, when the final map was presented to City of Lapu-lapu for its conformity, Mayor Raclaza still refused to sign for the reason that the city is not amenable to the DENR's opinion, thus the undersigned executed an affidavit as required by DENR for the acceptance and approval of the survey;" The aforementioned terminal report and the affidavit executed by Geodetic Engineer/Contractor Fernando B. Gurrea concretely and sufficiently documented Lapu- lapu City's refusal to accept the DENR Boundary Survey Result. Such refusal is the disagreement referred to as "bounclary dispute" contemplated under Rule III, Article 15, of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the LGC.

Be that as it may, the acknowledgement of the Municipality of Cordova, Cebu, and that of DENIR, concerning LapuAapu City's disagreement to the boundary result creates an undisputed fact that indeed a boundary dispute exists. I-laving established the existence ofa boundary dispute, the Department moves on to assess herein request for reconsideration of DILG Legal Opinion No. 26 dated 20 December 2016. It is noticeable that the letter dated 13 October 2016 that was responded to by DILG Legal Opinion No. 26 dated 20 December 2016 requested this Department's enforcement of the subject DENR Boundary Survey Result. Contrariwise, the plea added to this standing request for reconsideration is for this Department to allow DENR's implementation of said boundary survey result. Nonetheless, be it the department enforcing said boundary survey result or be it the DENIR implementing it in cooperation with this Department, both courses of actions are procedurally infirm. The LGC provides that the jurisdictional responsibility for the settlement of boundary disputes lies with the respective legislative councils of the contending local government units, to wit: "SECTION 118. Jurisdictional Responsibility for Settlement Of Boundary Dispute. - Boundary disputes between and among local government units shall, as much as possible, be settled amicably. To this end: (a) Boundary disputes involving two (2) or more Barangays in the same city or municipality shall be referred for settlement to the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned. (b) Boundary disputes involving two (2) or more municipalities within (he same province Shal] be referred for settlement to the Sangguniang Panlala "'igan concerned. (c) Boundary disputes involving municipalities or component cities of different provinces shall be jointly referred for settlement to the Sanggunians of the pro vinces concerned. (d) Boundary disputes involving a component city or municipality on the one hand and a highly urbanized city on the other, or two (2) or more highly urbanized cities, shall be jointly referred for settlement to the respective Sanggunians of the pa rties.

(e) 111 the event the Sanggunian fails to effect an amicable settlement within sixty (60) days from the date the dispute was referred thereto, it shall issue a certification to that effect. Thereafter, the dispute shall be formally tried by the Sanggunian concerned which shall decide the issue within sixty (60) days from the date of the certification referred to above. In case the attempt for amicable settlement before the sanggunian failed, a certification shall be issued to that effect, and the dispute shall be formally tried by the Sanggunian concerned within 60 clays from the date of the aforementioned certification. In this regard, Lhe sanggunian is specifically vested with original jurisdiction to actually hear and decide the dispute pursuant to the procedures laid down in the Local Government Code of 1991 and its implementing rules and regulations. Only upon failure of these intermediary steps will resort to the RTC having jurisdiction over the area in dispute follow, as specifically provided in Sec. 119, which reads: "SECTION 119. Appeal. - Within the time and manner prescribed by the Rules of Court, any party may elevate the decision of the Sanggunian concerned to the proper Regiohal Trial Court having jurisdiction over the area in dispute. The Regional Trial Court shall decide the appeal within one (I) year from the filing thereof. Pending final resolution of the disputed area prior to the dispute shall be maintained and continued for all legalpurposes. ' The foregoing provision gives the dissatisfied party an avenue to question the decision of the Sanggunian concerned to the Regional Trial Court. Thus, all the more negates the possibility ror this Department to have jurisdiction over boundary disputes. Accordingly, it can be inferred from the implementing rules and regulations of the LGC that the involvement of this Department in these cases is limited to being mere custodian of all relevant documents concerning boundary disputes brought before local sanggunians. It is specifically provided in Article 19, Rule III, IRR of' the LGC, which reads: 'ARTICLE 19. Official Custodian. — The DILG shall be the official custodian of copies of all documents on boundary disputes of LGUs. " Now, therefore, it is based on the preceding context that herein request for reconsideration is hereby resolved in the negative. While we are on this, hbwever, the Department assures you of the assistance it may provide within the bounds permitted by law and its mandate. Please be informed that the chief executives of the local governments of Lapu-Lapu City and the Municipality of Cordova Cebu were already informed of the available remedies concerning the boundaries of their respective territories.

Corollarily, in line with this Department's supervisory function over local governments, the LGUs of Cordova, Cebu, and Lapu-lapu City shall be directed to comply with Section 118(d) and (e) of the Local Government Code, and Rule III of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991 without prejudice to judicial recourse, as provided in the Local Government Code. Please be assured of our prompt action on this matter. Thank you. Ver AUS ly yours, ERO Undersecretary DILG- OUSLG 201 0 •O' 2 Legul/8a
